Borrowed from American English bingo (“bingo”), originally the cry used by a player upon winning. The English word is of uncertain origin, perhaps an extension of bing, an imitative word suggesting the ringing of a bell; compare the use of bingo! as an exclamation of sudden realization or success.

1000608.etyen:
From Den (“the”) + sentralafrikanske (“Central African”) + republikk (“republic”), literally “the Central African republic”. According to NAOB, sentralafrikansk (“Central African”) is modelled on English Central African; compare the country's official French name République centrafricaine (“Central African Republic”).
Parallel formations include Swedish Centralafrikanska republiken, German Zentralafrikanische Republik, Dutch Centraal-Afrikaanse Republiek and English Central African Republic.

1004704.etyen:
From Charlotte (“female given name”) + lund (“grove, wood”), with linking/genitive -n-, literally “Charlotte’s grove”. The Trondheim place name comes from the estate Charlottenlund, separated from Grilstad in 1854 and named after Charlotte Amalie, a daughter of the owner Michael Voigt. The Danish place name likewise comes from Charlottenlund slott (“Charlottenlund Palace”), named after Princess Charlotte Amalie of Denmark.
